messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Julian Park <julian.park@orbitai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: OrbitAI — usage-backed GPU top-up & SLA staging

Hi Julian,

Hope you had a good week — quick follow on our renewal conversation. We dug into the telemetry you shared and pulled Q3 utilization to validate sizing options. I attached a short CSV with slot-level utilization (OrbitAI_utilization_Q3.csv) and a draft SLA we've used for similar short-term stagings (SLA-proposal_v2.pdf).

Quick summary:
- Peak sustained slot utilization hit ~78% over a 2-week window in Oct (models with long KV cache replays).
- 95th-percentile latency spikes correlated to burst traffic on weekdays.

Based on that, two pragmatic paths we typically recommend for accounts in your position:
1) Add a short-term tranche (40 additional A100-equivalent GPUs) effective Jan 1 to cover Q1 traffic and avoid throttling while we rightsize model footprints.
2) Increase committed capacity by ~30% across your Dedicated fleet with a staged rollout + a month of burst credits for immediate headroom.

Neither option requires model re-architecture immediately — both buy runway while we collaborate on batching/kv-cache configs. Can you confirm preferred timing and whether procurement needs a formal cost-impact workbook? If so I can loop in pricing and drop a modeled P&L.

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0162

Attachments: OrbitAI_utilization_Q3.csv; SLA-proposal_v2.pdf
From: Julian Park <julian.park@orbitai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orbitai.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OrbitAI — usage-backed GPU top-up & SLA staging

Michael,

Thanks for the analysis and the CSV — that lines up with what we've been seeing. A few notes from our side:
- We expect a product launch in late Jan that will drive a ~25-35% increase in inference TPS for the first 10 weeks.
- Our finance team prefers a short-term top-up over increasing long-term commits; they want a clear 90-day runway.
- Procurement asked for a modeled cost impact and an explicit amendment draft for our legal review.

Request: can Redwood provision an additional 40 GPUs (A100-equivalent) as a paid tranche from Jan 1–Mar 31, with an SLA bump to 99.5% for inference latency on burst traffic? If that's not possible we can discuss a 60-day staging instead.

I've attached our internal cost estimate (cost-impact-model.xlsx) for reference. Procurement will need an official amendment to start approvals.

Appreciate the quick help, Julian

--

Subject: Fwd: OrbitAI — usage-backed GPU top-up & SLA staging

Laura / Vivek — forwarding Orbit's ask. Key points: 40 A100-eq tranche Jan 1–Mar 31, they want a temporary SLA uplift (99.5% latency for bursts) and an amendment doc for procurement. Procurement is ready to start once they have modeling + a signed amendment.

Options I'm proposing:
A) Short-term tranche (40 GPUs) priced as a 3-month addendum, with automatic conversion credit toward committed capacity if they convert within 90 days. No long-term pricing change.
B) 30% commit increase with a 3-month free burst buffer (50 GPUs) to smooth launch traffic — requires a longer sales/cfo approval but gives better unit economics.
C) Immediate burst buffer (50 GPUs) for 30 days to cover launch window, followed by evaluation.

Questions for you: pricing for option A (list + margin) and whether we can offer the 99.5% latency SLA for a defined burst window without escalating to legal. Vivek, any concerns from the runtime side about provisioning 40 A100-eqs at the start of Jan and the rollback plan?

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 04 Dec 2027 10:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OrbitAI — usage-backed GPU top-up & SLA staging

All,

We can do Option A with a commercial construct that meets both procurement and ops constraints. Proposed mutual action plan:
1) Redwood issues a 3-month paid tranche for 40 A100-eq GPUs (Jan 1–Mar 31) at the attached rates. If Orbit converts to a committed increase before Mar 31, we credit 50% of tranche fees toward the new commit for the first 12 months.
2) SLA: we can extend our latency SLA to 99.5% for burst windows (defined: peak traffic hours 09:00–18:00 PT) for the tranche period. This is conditional on Orbit adopting our recommended batching/kv-cache config changes (Vivek will validate).
3) Vivek: Redwood ops will provision capacity in two waves to reduce risk (20 GPUs by Jan 1, further 20 by Jan 15) — if provisioning conflicts occur we'll route traffic to a burst pool in a secondary region.
4) Legal: I'm attaching a short amendment draft (amendment-draft.docx) and a DocuSign stub so Procurement can start approvals.

Next steps: Julian/procurement to confirm acceptance of the amendment terms + sign DocuSign by Dec 15 to meet Jan 1 provisioning. Vivek, please confirm provisioning schedule and any ops caveats by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
